r0060.title: trotzdem vs deshalb/deswegen – уступка и следствие
r0060.titleEn: trotzdem vs deshalb/deswegen - concession and consequence
r0060.content_md_en:
### Two connecting adverbs that get mixed up

deshalb / deswegen / darum / daher — consequence. There is a cause, and the result you would expect from it.
trotzdem — concession. The cause is there, but the result contradicts it.

Es regnet. Deswegen bleibe ich zu Hause. – It is raining. Therefore I am staying home. (as expected)
Es regnet. Trotzdem gehe ich spazieren. – It is raining. Nevertheless I am going for a walk. (against expectation)

### A one-question test
Substitute "therefore". If the meaning still works, you need deswegen/deshalb. If "anyway / nevertheless" fits better, you need trotzdem.

### The link to Nebensatz conjunctions
Each adverb has a matching subordinating conjunction. One idea, two ways to say it:
weil (because) - deshalb / deswegen (therefore)
obwohl (although) - trotzdem (nevertheless)

Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil es regnet. = Es regnet. Deswegen bleibe ich zu Hause.
Ich gehe spazieren, obwohl es regnet. = Es regnet. Trotzdem gehe ich spazieren.

### Word order
trotzdem, deshalb, deswegen are adverbs, not conjunctions. They take position 1, the verb stays in position 2, and the subject moves after the verb:
Trotzdem gehe ich spazieren. (not "Trotzdem ich gehe")
Deswegen bleibe ich zu Hause. (not "Deswegen ich bleibe")

⚠ weil and obwohl are subordinating conjunctions - the verb goes to the end of the Nebensatz. deshalb and trotzdem are adverbs - the verb stays in second position. Positions are covered in the rule "Sentence positions".
r0060.examplesEn:
Es regnet. Deswegen bleibe ich zu Hause. – It is raining. Therefore I am staying home.
Es regnet. Trotzdem gehe ich spazieren. – It is raining. Nevertheless I am going for a walk.
Er hat viel gearbeitet. Trotzdem ist er nicht müde. – He worked a lot. Nevertheless he is not tired.
Ich habe keine Zeit. Deshalb komme ich nicht. – I have no time. Therefore I am not coming.
Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil es regnet. – I am staying home because it is raining.
Ich gehe spazieren, obwohl es regnet. – I am going for a walk although it is raining.
r0060.noteEn: deshalb/deswegen mark a consequence (the pair to weil), trotzdem marks a concession (the pair to obwohl). Both are adverbs, not conjunctions: position 1, verb in position 2, inversion.

r0061.title: Genitiv Plural – один артикль на все роды
r0061.titleEn: Genitiv Plural - one article for every gender
r0061.content_md_en:
### Genitiv Plural - one article for every gender

In the plural, gender disappears. The article in the Genitiv Plural is always der, no matter what gender the word has in the Singular.

Nominativ Plural: die Männer / die Frauen / die Kinder
Genitiv Plural: der Männer / der Frauen / der Kinder

### The noun itself does not change
Unlike the Singular, no -(e)s ending is added in the Genitiv Plural:
Singular: des Mannes, des Hauses
Plural: der Männer, der Häuser

This is also what separates the Genitiv Plural from the Dativ Plural, where -n is obligatory:
Dativ Plural: mit den Kindern, mit den Häusern
Genitiv Plural: die Farbe der Kinder, das Dach der Häuser

### With possessive and negative articles
The ending is -er, the same as on the article der:
die Bücher meiner Kinder – my children's books
die Wohnung unserer Freunde – our friends' flat
die Rechte keiner Bürger werden verletzt – no citizens' rights are being violated
die Stimmen aller Wähler – all the voters' votes

### After prepositions that take the Genitiv
The same prepositions as in the Singular (wegen, trotz, während, statt/anstatt, außerhalb/innerhalb), only the article is der:
wegen der Kinder – because of the children
trotz der Probleme – despite the problems
während der Ferien – during the holidays

⚠ Do not confuse der in the Genitiv Plural with der in the Nominativ Singular masculine - only the context tells them apart: der Mann kommt (Nom. Sg.) vs die Bücher der Männer (Gen. Pl.)

⚠ Forming the Genitiv Singular by gender, weak declension and proper names are covered in the separate rule "Genitiv Singular".
r0061.examplesEn:
die Rechte der Bürger – the citizens' rights
die Farbe der Häuser – the colour of the houses
das Ende der Ferien – the end of the holidays
die Bücher meiner Freunde – my friends' books
wegen der Kinder – because of the children
trotz der Probleme – despite the problems
während der Verhandlungen – during the negotiations
r0061.noteEn: Genitiv Plural: the article der for every gender, and the noun takes no ending (unlike the Genitiv Singular, and unlike the Dativ Plural with -n). Complements the rule "Genitiv Singular".
